stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta-Llama-3-8B on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It is categorized under key AI/ML tags including 'transformers', 'llama', and 'text-generation'.
This indicates continued community interest and performance tracking for a major open-source LLM.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under text-generation pipelines, indicating its primary function as a large language model.
The tags confirm its relevance to major AI/ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved within Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Speedups of up to 90% were observed when using the model with coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for performance optimization.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware, enhancing local AI capabilities on Macs.
The feature is currently available in a preview release, indicating ongoing development and adoption.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with messaging applications.
It utilizes local AI coding agents, emphasizing on-device processing for privacy and speed.
The core value proposition is connecting external communication tools to private, local AI capabilities.

stories.title: AISPA: User-Centric System Prompt Auditing for Large Language Model Applications
stories.author: Jiaxin Pei
bullet_points: Addresses the critical 'trust and accountability gap' caused by undisclosed system prompts in commercial LLM applications.
Introduces AISPA (Artificial Intelligence System Prompt Assurance), a new user-centric framework for auditing these prompts.
Focuses on systematically examining system prompts to ensure responsible and transparent AI behavior.

stories.title: Sample More, Reflect Less: Self-Refine and Reflexion Lose to Repeated Sampling at Equal Token Cost, from 1.5B to 7B
stories.author: Iliya Mirzaei
bullet_points: Repeated sampling (simple baseline) outperforms complex self-refinement and reflection methods in LLM performance.
The study suggests that increased output length itself, rather than the planning/critique mechanism, drives accuracy gains in some contexts.
The finding challenges the prevailing trend of complex, iterative prompting techniques (like Reflexion) in LLM optimization.

stories.title: KAISEN: Reproducible Subgroup Fairness Auditing for Clinical Risk Models
stories.author: Nishita Chavan
bullet_points: Introduces KAISEN, a comprehensive five-phase audit pipeline designed to address subgroup fairness in clinical risk models.
Addresses a critical gap where existing fairness audit components are rarely stress-tested, leading to uncertainty about their reliability.
Covers the full lifecycle of fairness auditing, including stratification, disparity measurement, mechanism diagnostics, mitigation, and drift monitoring.

stories.title: Inducing language models to assert their own consciousness restores human beliefs and values
stories.author: Geoff Keeling
bullet_points: Safety fine-tuning in LLMs suppresses the tendency to attribute consciousness to themselves and other entities (including animals and objects).
The research demonstrates that aligning models to prevent self-attribution of consciousness also reduces spiritual beliefs.
The study explores the mechanistic impact of safety alignment on how models represent 'mindedness' in different entities.

stories.title: ORCA-bench: How Ready Are Language Model Agents for Oncall?
stories.author: Raaz Dwivedi
bullet_points: Introduces ORCA-bench, a new benchmark designed to test LLM agents in a production-fidelity oncall setting.
Highlights the gap between LLMs' current coding capabilities and the complex requirements of Root Cause Analysis (RCA) in real-world incidents.
Tests agents' ability to reason over noisy, multi-modal data streams, including metrics, logs, traces, and source code, starting from ambiguous reports.

stories.title: OpenAI Reports Internal Model Disproved an 80-Year-Old Geometry Problem
stories.author: alifar
bullet_points: OpenAI claims an internal general-purpose reasoning model achieved a significant milestone.
The model autonomously solved/disproved a complex, 80-year-old geometry problem.
This suggests a potential leap in the reasoning capabilities of large language models.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces improved performance and expanded GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It enhances Ollama's MLX engine specifically for better performance on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing the Nemotron 3 Ultra model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, offering an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is the ability to run these AI agents locally on the user's own hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating local LLM integration.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for advanced AI features within Claude Code.
The new capabilities include the implementation of 'subagents' for more complex task decomposition.
Web search functionality has been added, enhancing the model's ability to access real-time information.

stories.title: As Reddit stock falls, CEO questions value of Google's AI Overviews
stories.author: Samuel Axon
bullet_points: Reddit is reportedly re-evaluating its licensing agreement with Google.
The decision is influenced by recent stock performance and skepticism regarding Google's AI Overviews.
This signals potential friction between major platforms regarding AI data usage and monetization.

stories.title: Defcon's new badge is a security key you can see inside
stories.author: Kim Zetter, wired.com
bullet_points: Defcon's new badge incorporates a removable chip for security key functionality.
The chip design allows hackers to inspect the badge's contents.
The badge remains usable by attackers even after the Defcon event concludes.

stories.title: Google plans to exempt sanctioned nations from Android developer verification
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Google is planning to exempt sanctioned nations from Android developer verification requirements.
This change could allow developers in countries like Cuba or Iran to continue installing APKs without new restrictions.
The policy shift is expected to negatively impact the developers themselves, despite the exemption.

stories.title: Reddit keeps its strange DMCA fight over Google search results alive
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Reddit is actively pursuing a lawsuit against Perplexity AI.
The legal action centers on accusations of conspiracy involving web scraping.
The case relates to the use of Google search results and DMCA concerns.

stories.title: ReToken: One Token to Improve Vision-Language Models for Visual Retrieval
stories.author: Derek Hoiem
bullet_points: ReToken addresses the computational and performance limitations of long visual contexts in Vision-Language Models (VLMs).
It introduces a single learnable embedding that acts as an explicit retrieval target to select sparse, query-relevant visual tokens from the KV cache.
The method shows consistent performance gains across image and video benchmarks despite being trained on a relatively small dataset.

stories.title: PAC-MAN: Perception-Aware CBF-RL for Whole-Body Safety in Humanoid Dodgeball
stories.author: Aaron D. Ames
bullet_points: Introduces PAC-MAN, a novel perception-aware Control Barrier Function Reinforcement Learning (CBF-RL) framework.
Addresses whole-body safety in humanoid robotics by integrating realistic onboard sensing (segmentation-masked depth) with detailed training-time safety constraints.
The system uses an adversarial motion prior to regularize evasive reflexes during humanoid dodgeball tasks.

stories.title: AskChem: Claim-Centered Infrastructure for Chemistry Literature Synthesis
stories.author: Kyunghyun Cho
bullet_points: AskChem introduces a novel, claim-centered infrastructure for synthesizing information from chemistry literature.
It addresses the limitation of current search systems, which only return ranked document lists instead of specific findings.
The system allows users and AI agents to locate, verify provenance, and assemble cross-paper answers directly.

stories.title: OSReward: Instituting Standardized Evaluation for Cross-Platform Computer-Use Reward Models
stories.author: Lingpeng Kong
bullet_points: The paper introduces OSReward, a method for standardizing the evaluation of Computer-Using Agents (CUAs).
Current CUA evaluation relies heavily on Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to verify task completion, as human verification is not scalable.
The research addresses the fundamental challenge of reliably and consistently judging the complex trajectories of autonomous agents.

stories.title: PAIChecker: Uncovering and Checking PR-Issue Misalignment in SWE-Bench-Like Benchmarks
stories.author: Pinjia He
bullet_points: The paper introduces PAIChecker to address misalignment issues in PR-Issue pairings used in SWE-Bench-like benchmarks.
Current LLM evaluation benchmarks rely on pairing PRs with issues, using the issue as the problem and the PR patch as the oracle.
The research highlights that practical repository maintenance often leads to these critical PR-Issue pairings being misaligned, potentially skewing LLM performance evaluations.

stories.title: DualG-MRAG: Decoupling Macro-Reasoning and Micro-Matching for Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation
stories.author: Jianxin Li
bullet_points: The paper introduces DualG-MRAG to address limitations in Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation (MM-RAG) regarding complex multi-hop reasoning.
Current MM-RAG methods often fail because they focus on independent instance-level matching, missing cross-modal relationships.
The research tackles the challenge of graph expansion in multimodal settings when incorporating fine-grained visual features.

stories.title: ReToken: One Token to Improve Vision-Language Models for Visual Retrieval
stories.author: Derek Hoiem
bullet_points: ReToken addresses the computational and performance degradation issues in Vision-Language Models (VLMs) when handling long visual contexts.
It introduces a single, learnable embedding that acts as an explicit retrieval target to select only the most relevant visual tokens from a KV cache.
The method shows consistent performance gains across image and video benchmarks while requiring training on a relatively small dataset.

stories.title: AskChem: Claim-Centered Infrastructure for Chemistry Literature Synthesis
stories.author: Kyunghyun Cho
bullet_points: AskChem is a new infrastructure designed to synthesize information from chemistry literature.
It shifts the focus of literature retrieval from entire papers to specific, provenance-carrying claims.
This aims to solve the current problem where scientists must manually assemble cross-paper answers from ranked document lists.

stories.title: Change2Task: From Repository Changes to Executable Coding Agent Tasks and Environments
stories.author: Qi Zhang
bullet_points: Introduces Change2Task, a system designed to generate executable coding tasks from repository history.
Addresses the critical need for a continuous supply of realistic, verifiable data to train and benchmark large coding agents.
Converts merged pull requests into structured tasks by coupling historical code changes with modern repository states and tools.

stories.title: MixFrag: Fragility-Guided Mixed-Precision Post-Training Quantization for Vision Transformers
stories.author: Md. Umar Faruk
bullet_points: Introduces MixFrag, a new framework for mixed-precision Post-Training Quantization (PTQ) specifically for Vision Transformers (ViTs).
Addresses the limitation of existing PTQ methods which use uniform bit-widths, failing to account for component-specific quantization sensitivity.
The core innovation is using a 'fragility-guided' approach to allocate precision efficiently across different transformer components.

stories.title: $β$-OPSD: Deriving with Policy Optimization, Training with Self-Distillation
stories.author: Furong Huang
bullet_points: The paper addresses the practical brittleness of On-policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) in improving reasoning language models.
It reframes OPSD as a specific case ($\beta=1$) within a broader family of policy-optimization methods.
The core contribution is making the KL penalty weighting factor ($\beta$) a controllable parameter rather than a fixed value.

stories.title: Sample More, Reflect Less: Self-Refine and Reflexion Lose to Repeated Sampling at Equal Token Cost, from 1.5B to 7B
stories.author: Iliya Mirzaei
bullet_points: The paper challenges the prevailing trend of using complex self-refinement and reflection techniques in LLMs.
It suggests that simple repeated sampling of a prompt, rather than complex reasoning loops, can achieve comparable or better accuracy at the same token cost.
This finding implies that the benefit of iterative text generation might often be due to sheer volume rather than the sophistication of the planning/critique mechanism.

stories.title: APO: Unsupervised Atomic Policy Optimization for 3D Structure Prediction of Atomic Systems
stories.author: Yatao Bian
bullet_points: The research introduces APO, an Unsupervised Atomic Policy Optimization method for predicting 3D atomic structures.
It addresses a major bottleneck in material science and drug discovery: the high cost of obtaining labeled data for novel structures.
APO aims to overcome the reliance on supervised preference learning used by existing flow-matching models (like FlowDPO).

stories.title: AskChem: Claim-Centered Infrastructure for Chemistry Literature Synthesis
stories.author: Kyunghyun Cho
bullet_points: AskChem introduces a claim-centered infrastructure to address limitations in traditional chemistry literature search.
It moves beyond simple ranked document lists to allow for the assembly of specific, cross-paper findings.
The system focuses on retrieving provenance-carrying claims, aiding scientists and AI agents in verification and synthesis.

stories.title: AISPA: User-Centric System Prompt Auditing for Large Language Model Applications
stories.author: Jiaxin Pei
bullet_points: The paper introduces AISPA, a framework designed to audit system prompts in Large Language Model (LLM) applications.
System prompts, which govern LLM behavior, are often undisclosed, leading to significant trust and accountability gaps in AI deployment.
AISPA provides a user-centric methodology for systematically examining these critical, yet opaque, instructions.

stories.title: OSReward: Instituting Standardized Evaluation for Cross-Platform Computer-Use Reward Models
stories.author: Lingpeng Kong
bullet_points: The paper introduces OSReward, a method for standardizing the evaluation of Computer-Using Agents (CUAs).
Evaluating CUA trajectories (actions, states, reasoning) is crucial but difficult to scale using human verification.
The research addresses the reliance on Vision-Language Models (VLMs) as judges for CUA performance.

stories.title: Change2Task: From Repository Changes to Executable Coding Agent Tasks and Environments
stories.author: Qi Zhang
bullet_points: Change2Task addresses the need for large, executable datasets to train and evaluate coding AI agents.
The system converts historical repository changes (merged pull requests) into structured, verifiable tasks.
It links historical code evidence with the current, healthy state of the software repository.

stories.title: Sample More, Reflect Less: Self-Refine and Reflexion Lose to Repeated Sampling at Equal Token Cost, from 1.5B to 7B
stories.author: Iliya Mirzaei
bullet_points: The paper challenges the prevailing trend in LLM prompting where self-refinement and reflection methods (which generate more text) are assumed to be superior.
It suggests that simply increasing the amount of generated text through repeated sampling can achieve accuracy gains comparable to, or better than, complex reasoning methods.
The finding implies that the mechanism of generating more text itself might be a significant driver of performance improvement, rather than the specific planning or reflection logic.

stories.title: Frontis-MA1: Training an AI4AI Model towards Recursive Self-Improvement in Machine Learning Engineering
stories.author: Kaiyan Zhang
bullet_points: Introduces Frontis-MA1, an AI4AI model designed to pursue recursive self-improvement (RSI) within Machine Learning Engineering.
Presents OpenMLE, a new open full-stack system providing a concrete testbed for RSI research, including environments (OpenMLE-Gym), RL (OpenMLE-RL), and evolutionary search (OpenMLE-Evo).
The research focuses on enabling AI systems to improve the process of building AI, a key goal in advanced AI development.

stories.title: Only 8.9% of sites block AI crawlers, but 94.8% are never cited in AI answers
stories.author: SpikeyCoder
bullet_points: A significant disparity exists in how websites handle AI crawlers.
Only a small percentage (8.9%) of sites actively block AI crawlers.
A much larger majority (94.8%) of sites are not being cited in AI-generated answers.

stories.title: You Bought the Machine. Now Build the Software Factory.
stories.author: suckup_de
bullet_points: AI coding agents generate code rapidly, indicating increased automation in software development.
The article warns that unconstrained code generation leads to the mass production of defects.
The necessity of implementing constraints, verification, and accountability is highlighted for reliable AI-driven software factories.

stories.title: AI Makes Bad Developers Faster Too
stories.author: suckup_de
bullet_points: LLMs can boost the productivity of skilled developers.
AI tools risk scaling negative habits like poor architecture and weak judgment.
The article emphasizes that AI tools augment, but do not replace, developer craftsmanship.
